resources.string: Bass mode
COMBO strength
0 dB is the tested level. Lowering it reduces both harsh sounds and the bass feel.
Speaker protection cap (experimental)
Pushes the 100–500 Hz layer down only at the moments it goes above the level below. Use it to hear whether kick and bass distortion gets smaller. The original sound is not reduced.
Cap level
Lower values push down more often. Start listening at −24 dB.

COMBO follows bass families and calculates harmonic levels with a fixed formula. It uses a −5 dB output; you can lower its strength. Harmonics are available at 44.1 kHz (150.7 ms delay) and 48 kHz (148.8 ms delay).
This mode plays with its tested default EQ. The values below are not used for the sound now. This mode also lowers the original sound below 80 Hz by −6 dB (shown on the EQ curve).
Unlock EQ
Uses the values below for the sound, in this mode only
Unlock the EQ of this mode?

This mode was tuned and measured with its default EQ (layer level and peak limit). Changing the EQ goes outside that testing, and dropouts, booming and limiter behavior can change. The low-mid band cannot go above its default (+3 dB). EQ stays unlocked when you switch off and return to COMBO. Choose Reset and lock to restore the defaults and lock it again.
Unlock
Playing with an untested EQ. The low-mid band is used only up to its default (+3 dB).
Reset and lock
Returns all EQ values to the defaults
Off
COMBO virtual bass
COMBO supports 44.1 and 48 kHz. No harmonic layer is added at the current output rate.
